items.example_en: The whole family was there.
items.note: The soft sign plus я gives a y sound before the vowel.

items.example_en: My parents live in the countryside.
items.note: Plural only in this sense. родственники means relatives.

items.example_en: My brother is younger than me.
items.note: Irregular plural: братья.

items.example_en: I have two sisters.
items.note: After 2, 3, 4 the noun takes the genitive singular: две сестры.

items.example_en: Their son started school.
items.note: Irregular plural: сыновья.

items.example: В воскресенье едем к бабушке и дедушке.
items.example_en: On Sunday we're going to our grandparents'.
items.note: к plus dative means towards or to someone's place.

items.example_en: My husband cooks better than I do.
items.note: жена is wife. женщина is woman, a different word.

items.example: Я иду в кино со своей девушкой.
items.example_en: I'm going to the cinema with my girlfriend.
items.note: With a possessive it means girlfriend; on its own, a young woman. Also how you address a waitress.

items.example_en: She's been married for ten years.
items.note: A man is женат. The two are not interchangeable.

items.example_en: He's a close friend of mine.
items.note: Irregular plural друзья. A woman friend is подруга.

items.example_en: That's just an acquaintance, not a friend.
items.note: Russians draw a sharp line between друг and знакомый.

items.example_en: I get along well with my sister.
items.note: с takes the instrumental: с сестрой.

items.example_en: She is tall and slim.
items.note: Adjectives agree: высокий, высокая, высокое, высокие.

items.example_en: He has short dark hair.
items.note: волосы is plural. Possession uses у него, not он имеет.

items.example: У неё зелёные глаза, как у матери.
items.example_en: She has green eyes, like her mother.
items.note: Singular глаз, plural глаза with a stress shift.

items.example_en: My colleague wears round glasses.
items.note: очки is plural only. носить is habitual; надеть is the one-off act of putting on.

items.example_en: You look tired.
items.note: The following adjective goes into the instrumental: усталым.

items.example_en: She looks a lot like her father.
items.note: Short adjective, agreeing with the subject: похож, похожа, похожи.

items.example_en: The neighbour is a very kind person.
items.note: The same root as in доброе утро.

items.example_en: Your brother is a lot of fun.
items.note: The ё is always stressed, and always written that way in learners' texts.

items.example_en: It's a very hard-working team.
items.note: Built from труд (labour) and любить (to love).

items.example_en: He's as stubborn as a donkey.
items.note: The Russian comparison uses a donkey, not a mule.

items.example_en: She's in a good mood today.
items.note: в plus prepositional. The opposite: в плохом настроении.

items.example: Несмотря ни на что, у неё хороший характер.
items.example_en: In spite of everything, she has a good temperament.
items.note: персонаж is a character in a story.

items.example_en: I'm glad to see you.
items.note: Short adjective: рад, рада, рады.

items.example_en: That news makes me sad.
items.note: Impersonal: мне грустно, literally to me it is sad.

items.example_en: I'm tired, I'm going to sleep.
items.note: Literally the past tense of устать, to get tired. A woman says устала.

items.example_en: I'm afraid of flying.
items.note: Reflexive verb, and its object takes the genitive: боюсь темноты.

items.example_en: I'm fed up with this noise.
items.note: The thing is the subject and agrees with it: надоел, надоела, надоело.

items.example_en: I get nervous before meetings.
items.note: перед takes the instrumental.

items.example_en: He quit? No way!
items.note: Friendly disbelief. ладно on its own means fine, all right.

items.example_en: Seriously? I didn't know.
The rain stopped? So much the better.
items.note: The instrumental тем plus a comparative.

items.example_en: Will you come? It depends when.
items.note: смотря plus a question word is the Russian it depends.

items.example: У меня всё хорошо, а ты?
items.example_en: I'm doing fine, and you?
items.note: а contrasts, и adds. Using и here would sound wrong.

items.example_en: Anyway, we had a good time.
items.note: Literally shorter. Everywhere in spoken Russian.
